findings.claim: Commit 2f281e85 moved each Your task block from the reading column to the head of the workspace card, but two step texts still describe the old position. Activity 1 step 1 says to read the code "in the workspace on the right (below these steps on a narrow screen)", and the last activity (line 700) says "in the workspace on the right"; the steps now sit inside that workspace at every width and the code is directly below them at both 1280 and 390 px, so the narrow-screen qualifier is wrong at wide widths and "on the right" is self-referential (and false on a narrow screen). The recap text-alternative repeats the same wording. Related: the h3 Your task now precedes the workspace h2 (visually hidden "Workspace:" prefix), so a learner jumping by level-2 heading to the workspace lands below the task. Reproduced by static read and a JS-enabled Chromium layout read at 1280 and 390 px.
findings.recommendation: Reword these Where to look steps (and their text-alternative copies) to name the place relative to the steps, for example the code or question directly below these steps, and either make Your task the workspace heading or place the workspace heading before it so heading navigation reaches the task first.

findings.claim: The new print rule reveals hidden activities only through section[data-pep-activity], and the recap section (line 745) has no such marker. With JavaScript on, printing from any activity before the recap prints every activity but omits the recap: its key points, cheat sheet, activity-procedures text alternative and sources. With JavaScript off, or when printing from the recap itself, the recap prints. Reproduced in JS-enabled Chromium with print media emulated on activity 1 (all activity sections, tasks and teaching visible; [data-pep-recap] not rendered) and in JS-disabled Chromium print media (recap rendered).
findings.recommendation: Extend the print rule to the recap section (for example by also matching the stage step container or a recap marker) so a printed page always includes the recap, and add the recap to the print assertion.

findings.claim: The diff removed the branch that cleared data-pep-complete when leaving the recap, and the attribute is now written only when the recap is shown. restart() returns early on the recap and otherwise calls show() for a non-recap step, so after a learner reaches the recap with every activity passed, goes back and presses Restart activity on a passed activity, that section correctly drops to completed=false and credit 0, but main keeps data-pep-complete="true" until the recap is visited again. DESIGN.md (State model) requires page completion to be false until the restarted activity passes again. The visible recap message is recomputed on return, so learner-visible text is unaffected; the stale value is in the completion hook that the QA harness also reads. Severity is low because the state is reachable only after the learner has already passed every activity once, no learner-visible claim is wrong, and per-activity completion, credit and grade hooks are correct. Established by static trace of restart(), show() and complete(); not exercised end-to-end because that needs graded answers.
findings.recommendation: Recompute data-pep-complete whenever per-activity completion changes (for example in progress() or restart()), keeping navigation-only moves from changing it, so Restart of a passed activity sets page completion false until it passes again.

items.note: Loop 3 on the bytes after commits fef86277 and 2f281e85. Verified from the unfiltered diff 77598a8a..2f281e85 that, on this page, the starter, EDITOR_CFG, inline python-scaffold@3 adapter, checker rules, TOPIC.need/obj maps and all learner-visible task, step, teaching and no-JS text are byte-unchanged; the only change touching the editor is removal of a stray data-pep-activity marker from its fieldset (the per-section state hooks select only section[data-pep-activity][id^=activity-], so completion wiring is unaffected). The Your task block and its activity checks now open the activity-4 workspace card, directly before the workspace heading, the supplied files and the editor in DOM order, and renders in that order in JS-disabled Chromium at 390 px. This loop did not re-read the checker rules: the pass requirements below rest on that byte-identity with what loops 1 and 2 read, on the current step text, and on the two rejections below. Activity 4 (Raise your own exceptions, #activity-4) still carries the required authoring task in the inventory.py lesson editor (fieldset #exed, goal "author", the only check for step 4). To pass, the learner must write a raise of the supplied custom exception with a non-empty message at the placeholder, then write handler, else and finally blocks aligned with try, each with its module-logger call, including the exception-logging call in the handler. That covers o1, o2 and o3 as construction rather than recognition, which is what the recommendation (a bounded scaffold with the supplied custom exception and provided module logger) asked for. Residual (not blocking this education finding): the step text names the clause keywords and logger method names quite literally, more literally than the reworded functions step; the learner still has to compose the message, the clause order and placement, indentation and each logger call, so it is guided construction rather than pure transcription. Whether to reword toward goals is an SME/authoring choice, not a reopening of this finding. Gating re-verified in JS-enabled Chromium: a fresh load with an #activity-4 fragment is normalised to #activity-1, the locked activity-4 timeline link and a manual #activity-5 hash change leave the learner on activity 1 (or the current activity), and Continue stays hidden; running (programmatically, on the hidden and still-locked activity-4 editor) the untouched starter, and a variant with every placeholder replaced by pass, leaves data-pep-completed=false on the fieldset and on the activity-4 section. TOPIC.need step 4 is author only, and page completion requires every activity passed. A passing completion was not exercised (no protected input written).
